aggregate.detectors_note: A detector's denominator (`answerable_for`) is the labelled flags it was answerable for: every flag it spoke on with no `blame` (§5.4's rule that whatever raised an unwanted flag shares the charge), plus the flags whose `blame` named it. A flag whose `blame` named other detectors is not charged here, and one blamed on `score` is in no detector's denominator at all — so these denominators do not sum to the corpus total, by design. `spoke` is the wider count (every flag at this cut whose findings included this detector's) and is shown so the narrow one reads as a share of it. A detector with `g3: null` raised nothing here, which is no evidence rather than a clean bill of health (ADR-001 §7.7); `defaults.never_fired` names them.

tau_sweep.note: §5.4's `F(tau,W)` read at every threshold on the grid, over every episode: the flag population the threshold raises, the `G3` the hand-authored labels can answer for at it, the miss rate it produces, and `unlabelled` — flags nobody has read, which is what refuses to become a rate. This is where a published default is chosen or confirmed from; `thresholds.json` states the bar and the gate, and nowhere else does τ move.

formulas.labelling_note: ADR-001 §5.4 names §5.4's four false-positive codes as `expected`, `not-applicable`, `low-stakes` and `false-positive`. The closed list that actually shipped is `e4.6`'s (`fathom_analyze::queue::REASONS`), and the mapping is a collapse, not an invention: §5.4's `expected` is shipped `intentional` ("what looks risky here is what I wanted"); §5.4's `low-stakes` and `false-positive` are shipped under their own names; §5.4's `not-applicable` has no separate shipped code — `false-positive`'s claim ("the finding that raised this does not describe my change") already covers the case, so the two measure together and this file says so instead of hiding the collapse. §5.4's true positive `accepted-with-required-change` is shipped `accepted`: `e4.6`'s ledger has no 'with required change' refinement, so a flag that earned a review that happened is the true positive, and rework of the episode counts as one too per §5.4's own `TP(e)` clause. The five shipped codes that are neither (`not-my-area`, `already-known`, `superseded`, `will-revert`, `other`) are dismissals about the reviewer's attention or the queue's state rather than about the flag: they sit in `G3`'s denominator exactly as §5.4 writes it — the reviewer looked, so the flag cost something — and never in its numerator.

formulas.tau_note: §5.4 tightens the *rate* at 1.0 (0.15), not the threshold: tau stays 40 in both gates, so the two `g3-*` gates are one flag set read against two bars. This number moved from 70 to 40 in `reco-6co` and it moved *here*, in ADR-001 §5.4, in the shipped `risk.tau` default, in `fathom.toml` and in the reference policy in the same commit: §5.4 always said its default was to be "confirmed against three real OSS repositories", and the confirmation is this file's own measurement — nothing in 540 real episodes reached 70, so the τ arm of `F(τ,W)` was inert, while τ 40 was the corpus's own top-decile floor and remains the lowest threshold on the grid whose flags are all labelled (see `tau_sweep` in the blessed report). The deciles have moved twice since — 34 / 42 / 43 after `reco-0er` lifted every score by taking an absent axis out of the denominator, and 33 / 39 / 42 after `reco-l9bz.7` added an axis and re-spread the weights — so what binds τ is the labelling floor, not the deciles. The harness's check against the shipped `risk.tau` is what catches a copy that drifted.

gates.claim: at §5.4's published default τ — 40, confirmed against real history by this corpus in `reco-6co` — the aggregate false-positive rate clears the alpha gate
gates.why: Measured 0.608 (31 false positives on 51 labelled flags) against a bar of 0.30, and the number means something now, which is the difference between this read and `e4.9`'s. At τ 70 the flag arm was inert: 6 episodes in 540 reached it, all six through a high-severity finding and none through τ, because `features-1`'s ceiling on this corpus is 66. τ 40 is §5.4's own "confirmed against three real OSS repositories" — it is the shipped `risk.tau`, and the flag population is 51 episodes (9.4 % of the corpus), every one of them carrying a hand-authored disposition. What τ is no longer is the corpus's top-decile floor: the per-repository cuts are 32 / 39 / 41 and two of them now sit above τ. `reco-ydek.5` took the `authorship` axis out of `features-2` and paid `findings` and `surface` for it, and left this gate byte-identical: the same 51 episodes, the same 31 false positives, the same 0.608. That is not the change doing nothing — 24 of the 51 moved by a point or two — it is the change moving them sideways: the axis scored an author label this corpus's history almost never evidenced, so removing it redistributed a term most episodes were paying a flat rate for, and no episode was within two points of 40 on the strength of it. `aggregate.tau_sweep` is still the evidence and the floor: τ 40 is the lowest threshold on the grid whose flags are all labelled — at τ 35 seven of 66 are not — which is what makes this rate an answer about 51 episodes rather than an answer about 66.

gates.claim: across every episode the corpus flagged — §5.4's published τ plus each repository's own top-decile cut, which is what a reviewer would actually have been shown — no more than 30 % of the labelled flags were cost without value
gates.why: Measured 0.619 on 63 labelled flags: 26 dismissed `low-stakes` (Dependabot, renovate and release-bot bumps, and `update dev dependencies` episodes that re-emit the CI workflow templates and a 1 000-line lockfile — the workflow and dependency axes raised them and no finding justified them), 9 `false-positive` (a test spy charged as untested new logic, `# type: ignore` and `#[expect(deprecated)]` suppressions whose reason is written on the line above them, a `"TODO"` that is the name of a GitHub label, a fuzzer's own report charged as leftover debug output, and mdtest — ty's real test surface — counted as no tests at all), and 4 `intentional` (the `gh repo garden` deletion that took its test file with it, dropping Python 3.10 and the other end-of-life Pythons, and a `cli` recorder-buffering fix whose skipped vendored-skill tests were the point). 20 of the 39 false positives were blamed on the ranking rather than on a detector (`aggregate.coverage.blamed_on_score`), and the four that left are the four `reco-ydek.5`'s re-score took out of `cli`: bot-authored episodes were the ones the `authorship` axis was paying, so the band that had sat at exactly `cli`'s old cut of 33 scored 31 under `features-3` and fell under a cut that had itself dropped only to 32 — while the one episode the lower cut promoted was `accepted`. That is the whole of the 0.642 → 0.619 movement, and it is a denominator moving, not a ranking getting truer. The finding still stands and it is still about where the flags come from: the majority of what is left is human-authored maintenance that re-emits CI from an out-of-tree template, which no path rule can see.

gates.claim: no detector is disqualified by `e0.12`'s rule as this harness scores it: a default-enabled detector whose own false-positive rate breaches the alpha gate on at least 8 answerable flags (the bar a default flip has to clear, deliberately higher than the 5 a printed number has to clear) is a detector that must ship disabled. Read `why` before reading the 0 as a clean bill of health.
gates.why: Measured 0 enabled detectors that breached α with 8 or more flags, on the flag population of 63. Read §4 of the calibration page before trusting the sentence: every enabled detector answers 100 % of its flags and the seven zero-severity ones cannot enter this metric at all, so `pass` here means "no enabled detector was measured to be bad", which is not "the detectors are calibrated".

how_gates_are_set: Every gate declares `expected`: `pass`, `fail` or `not-measurable`. A gate that surprises us in either direction fails the run, because a claim that quietly starts passing has to be re-read just as hard as one that fails. The `fail` gates are the measurement's findings, not its defects: on three real OSS repositories — three windows of 180 episodes each, 540 episodes, 525 of them mature — the shipped score at §5.4's published default τ flags 51 episodes and 31 of them were cost without value, so the α gate measures 0.608; across everything the corpus flags at either cut, 67 flags of which 43 were cost without value, `G3` 0.642; and 20 of the 24 episodes that were mature and later needed rework still sat below τ, a miss rate of 0.833. Those are the numbers `e0.12`'s thresholds have to survive; they are written here rather than smoothed into a sentence. A gate is never adjusted to fit a measurement: the `min_denominator` floor is what turns an anecdote into `not-measurable` instead of into a comfortable `pass`, and when a gate's `expected` changed it changed because the measurement moved — `miss-rate-denominator-is-big-enough` at the `reco-dyt` re-pin (7 → 24 mature reworked episodes), and `every-flagged-episode-is-labelled` twice, where `reco-6co`'s re-score promoted one episode into the flag population and `reco-0zi`'s re-measure — after `reco-0er` took a guessed `human` out of the score's denominator — promoted five: in both cases the promoted diffs were read and written up before the run was blessed, and the gate came back to `pass`. The bars themselves — 0.30, 0.15, 0.20 — have never moved. `reco-l9bz.7` re-measured with a thirteenth feature axis and a sixth ranking component and moved no bar either: 51 of the 58 episodes the previous run had flagged changed score, nine came into a flag population for the first time, five left one, and four of the nine needed a fresh hand reading before the run could be blessed (§3e). Two of the seven numbers moved in the reviewer's favour and one moved against it, and the one that moved against it is quoted in full under `miss-rate-at-published-tau`.

what: The gates the Guardrail 3 calibration harness (`e4.9`, `reco-mkl.1`) holds its own measurement to. ADR-001 §5.4 publishes `G3 <= 0.30` at alpha, `<= 0.15` at 1.0 and `miss_rate <= 0.20`, and says out loud that `e4.3` and `m1` defer to "the threshold agreed in `e0.12`"; those numbers are copied into this file from §5.4 and nowhere else, and the harness refuses to run if the alpha threshold here disagrees with the shipped default `risk.tau` — one number, in the document, and a check that the copy did not drift. `cargo run -p fathom-analyze --features sqlite-bundled,langs-all --example g3_calibration -- --check` re-measures them against the three pinned repositories and fails if any gate came out other than declared. The `langs-all` is not decoration: since `reco-l9bz.7` the score carries a cyclomatic-complexity axis, and a build without the grammars silently leaves that axis out of every denominator on the corpus rather than failing.
